title: Not every opportunity is from God (1 Corinthians 10:23)
paragraphs: Not every opportunity is from God (1 Corinthians 10:23)
Not every open door came from God.

Some doors are profitable.
Some are exciting.
Some are legal.
Some are applauded.
“Everything is permissible,” Paul wrote, “but not everything is beneficial… not everything builds up” (1 Corinthians 10:23).

Because the question is not only, Can I do this?
The deeper question is, Will this draw me closer to Christ, or slowly pull me away?

The enemy does not always tempt with obvious evil.
Sometimes he offers a polished opportunity.
A bigger platform.
A faster paycheck.
A relationship that feels right.
A shortcut that looks harmless.

But here’s what we miss:
Not every blessing-looking thing is from the hand of God.
Some opportunities feed the flesh while starving the soul.

God is not just leading you into what is available.
He is leading you into what is obedient.

So before you say yes, pray.
Before you move, weigh it by Scripture.
Before you call it favor, ask whether it produces holiness, peace, and faithfulness.
Because a good opportunity can still become a bad decision when Jesus is not Lord over it.
And that’s where grace walks in.

Maybe you said yes too quickly.
Maybe you chased what glittered.
Maybe you called compromise “wisdom.”

Come back.
Christ does not shame the repentant.
He restores them.

Jesus is still able to redirect your steps, redeem your wrong turns, and teach your heart to desire what truly builds. His will is not a prison. It is protection. His commands are not chains. They are life.

So do not chase every open door.
Chase the Shepherd.
